topic.title: The boring D2C brands are the ones raising money
topic.claim: While Zepto's IPO got cut by 64%, a laptop-sleeve brand and an ayurveda skincare brand just raised large rounds, funding is quietly rotating toward products with real margins.
topic.behaviour: DailyObjects raised $34.3 million Series C, Nat Habit raised ₹142 crore Series C on ₹330 crore annualised revenue, D2C ecommerce brands collectively raised over $63 million in early October alone, and 180+ founders gathered at the Bharat D2C Conclave in Delhi to discuss offline retail and AI.
topic.mechanism: Investors burned by quick-commerce cash burn are rotating toward categories with repeat purchase and actual unit economics, even if the brand is less flashy than a 10-minute delivery app.
topic.group: anyone following startup and brand news, people building or buying from D2C brands
real_details: DailyObjects raised $34.3 million led by Xponentia Capital Partners, Anicut Capital and Axiom Asia Private Capital
Nat Habit raised ₹142 crore led by Trident Growth Partners, with annualised gross revenue of ₹330 crore
D2C ecommerce brands raised over $63 million in early October alone
180+ founders gathered at the Bharat D2C Conclave in Delhi on October 6
topic.news_peg: DailyObjects and Nat Habit funding rounds, Bharat D2C Conclave, October 2026
topic.why_now: landed the same month as Zepto's IPO reality check, a sharp contrast

score.why: Ties a big funding story to boring-margin brands, the same move as her 'real luxury is privacy' style reframe about where money quietly goes.
